mainTopic: Wooden versus earthenware כלי שרת, and the laws of מריקה ושטיפה for pots used to cook קדשים, including part of a vessel, which offerings it covers, and תרומה
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who accepts a כלי שרת made of wood, does not accept one made of earthenware. Then comes a story. רב יצחק בר יהודה left רמי בר חמא for רב ששת, because רב ששת answers from a משנה, while רמי answers from reasoning that one משנה can knock down. To test him, רב יצחק asks whether a pot used to cook a קרבן in only part of it needs מריקה ושטיפה in full. רמי says no and compares it to a garment splashed with blood. A ברייתא proves him wrong: the whole vessel needs it, and the source is the פסוק 'in a copper vessel'. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא that extends מריקה ושטיפה from חטאת to all קדשים, but not to תרומה, according to רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון limits it to קדשי קדשים. When a ברייתא shows that a תרומה pot does need cleaning, אביי, רבא and רבה בר עולא each explain that the פסוק frees תרומה from only one strict detail. Finally, a new משנה records רבי טרפון and חכמים arguing over how long a pot may be used during a רגל, and defines מריקה and שטיפה as done with cold water.

steps.title: Even the lenient view does not accept earthenware
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's lenient view to wooden vessels only, not earthenware.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה only said this about a vessel of wood. But about a vessel of earthenware, he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing an earlier discussion. It points out that even the most lenient opinion only allows wood, not earthenware.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is the one who accepts a כלי שרת made of wood, a material with some importance. The גמרא stresses that his leniency stops there. Earthenware is a cheap material, and nobody accepts it as a כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said..., a phrase that limits how far a ruling goes

steps.whatToRemember: Wood: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה accepts it as a כלי שרת. Earthenware: no one does.

phrases.english: And even Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
only said it about one of wood,
phrases.notes: 'One' here means a כלי שרת, a vessel used in the Temple service, which is what they've been talking about.

phrases.english: but about one of earthenware, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קָאָמַר אֶלָּא דְּעֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous part of the daf about which materials can serve as a כלי שרת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An earthenware vessel is not valid as a כלי שרת, even according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: A student leaves his teacher for another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story: רב יצחק בר יהודה used to learn before רמי בר חמא but left him for רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יהודה was used to learning in front of רמי בר חמא. He left him and went to רב ששת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story and sets the scene for the conversation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is being argued yet. We only learn who the people are and that the student switched teachers. That switch is what sparks the conversation.

keyTerms.meaning: He was used to learning in front of him

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה רְגִיל קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא,
phrases.english: was used to learning before Rami bar Chama,
he left him and went to Rav Sheshet.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יְהוּדָה הֲוָה רְגִיל קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story begins. It will lead into a question about מריקה ושטיפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Background only: רב יצחק בר יהודה switched from רמי בר חמא to רב ששת.

steps.title: The old teacher teases his former student
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא meets his former student and mocks him: do you think learning near רב ששת makes you like him?
steps.simpleTranslation: One day רמי בר חמא met him and said: When the tax chief grabbed me, did his good smell come onto my hand? Just because you went to learn before רב ששת, have you become like רב ששת?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא challenges his former student for leaving him, using a popular saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying means that being near a great person does not make you great. Holding a rich official's perfumed hand does not leave his smell on you. The question sounds like a question, but it is really a jab at the student.

keyTerms.meaning: A high official or tax chief
Grabbed me, took hold of me

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד פְּגַע בֵּיהּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: One day he met him and said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אַלְקַפְטָא נַקְטַן, רֵיחָא אָתֵי לַהּ לְיָד?!
phrases.english: The tax chief grabbed me, so the fragrance came to the hand?!
phrases.notes: A popular saying: touching an important man's perfumed hand doesn't give you his smell. Being near greatness doesn't make you great.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּאָזְלַתְּ לָךְ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: Because you went off to learn before Rav Sheshet,
have you become like Rav Sheshet?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְקַפְטָא נַקְטַן, רֵיחָא אָתֵי לַהּ לְיָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the student's decision from step 2 to switch teachers.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק בר יהודה's choice to leave רמי בר חמא for רב ששת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being near a great teacher does not by itself make you great, so the move seems pointless or arrogant.

steps.title: Why the student switched: answers from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק explains that he switched because רב ששת answers from a משנה, while רמי answers from his own reasoning, which a משנה can overturn.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: That is not the reason. You, master, answer my questions with your own reasoning. So when I find a משנה that says otherwise, it knocks down your answer. רב ששת answers my questions from a משנה. So even if I find another משנה that disagrees, it is just one משנה against another משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The student answers the jab. He switched because of how each teacher answers questions, not because he hoped to become great by being near רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer built on סברא is weaker. One משנה that disagrees refutes it completely. An answer built on a משנה has a source behind it, so a second משנה only creates a contradiction between two sources and does not wipe it out.

keyTerms.meaning: A משנה or ברייתא, a source from the תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: רב יצחק is not saying רמי's reasoning is bad. He is saying an answer based only on reasoning can be fully knocked down by a single משנה, while an answer backed by a משנה cannot.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of how the גמרא weighs arguments: a source from the תנאים outweighs logic alone.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is not because of that;
Master, when I ask about a matter,
you resolve it for me from reasoning;
when I find a משנה, it refutes it.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת – כִּי בָּעֵינָא מִילְּתָא מִינֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, when I ask a matter of him,
resolves it for me from a משנה;
so that even when you find a משנה that refutes it,
it is a משנה against a משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the real reason for the switch
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רמי thought the student left just to be near a famous teacher.
steps.terutzMaskana: He left because רב ששת's answers rest on a משנה and are harder to refute.

steps.title: The teacher offers to answer from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא invites the student to ask him a question, which he will answer like a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Ask me something, and I will answer it for you like a משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רמי accepts the challenge and opens the way for the actual question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי wants to show that he can also give answers backed by a source. This sets up the halachic question about מריקה ושטיפה.

keyTerms.meaning: That I will resolve for you

phrases.english: He said to him: Ask me a matter,
which I will resolve for you like a משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעִי מִינַּי מִילְּתָא, דְּאִיפְשִׁיט לָךְ כִּי מַתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the student's explanation in step 4 by offering a test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רמי offers to answer a question using a משנה as his source.

steps.title: Cooking in only part of a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The student asks: if a חטאת was cooked in only part of a vessel, does the whole vessel need מריקה ושטיפה?
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him: If someone cooked a חטאת in only part of a vessel, does it need מריקה ושטיפה, or does it not?
steps.whatsHappening: The student asks his halachic test question about scouring and rinsing a pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires a pot used to cook a חטאת to be scoured and rinsed. The question is whether this applies to the whole pot, or only to the part the meat actually touched.

phrases.english: He asked him:
If one cooked in part of a vessel,
phrases.notes: He means cooking the meat of a חטאת, which is what makes a vessel need scouring and rinsing.

phrases.aramaic: טָעוּן מְרִיקָה וּשְׁטִיפָה, אוֹ אֵין טָעוּן?
phrases.english: does it require scouring and rinsing, or does it not require it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The question that רמי invited in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the whole vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה when only part of it was used for cooking.

steps.title: Not needed, just like sprinkled blood
steps.stepSummary: רמי answers that the whole vessel does not need it, comparing this to הזאה, where only the stained part of the garment is washed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It does not need it. It is just like the case of sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי answers the question and backs it with a comparison to a משנה about blood sprinkled on a garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that when blood of a חטאת is sprinkled on a garment, only the stained spot needs washing. In the same way, only the part of the vessel used for cooking needs מריקה ושטיפה, not the whole vessel.
steps.whatToRemember: This is רמי בר חמא's proposed answer. It is overturned in steps 13–14, where a ברייתא rules that the whole vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה.

phrases.english: He said to him: It does not require it,
just as it is with sprinkling.
phrases.notes: This is the case of חטאת blood splashing onto a garment, where only the spot it landed on must be washed (93b).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵינוֹ טָעוּן, מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַהַזָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The whole vessel does not need מריקה ושטיפה, just as with הזאה only the stained part of the garment is washed.

steps.title: The student objects that no source says this
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יהודה points out that רמי בר חמא's answer is not actually taught in any משנה or ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא did not teach this!
steps.whatsHappening: The student challenges רמי: you promised to answer like a משנה, but no משנה says what you just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רמי promised his answer would be as solid as a משנה. The student now tests that promise and finds no written source behind the ruling. This sets up רמי's admission that he is reasoning on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, but surely (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But the tanna does not teach this!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7 for lacking a written source
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's ruling that only the cooked part of the vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He promised a משנה-level answer, but no משנה or ברייתא teaches it

steps.title: רמי בר חמא defends his answer as logical, based on the garment case
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא admits there is no explicit source but says it is logical: just as a garment is washed only where the blood landed, a vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה only where cooking happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It makes sense to compare it to a garment. Just as a garment needs washing only where the blood is, so too a vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה only where the cooking happened.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי answers that even without a source, his ruling follows logically from the law of a garment splashed with blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי builds a comparison: garment and vessel are both cleaned because of contact with a חטאת. Since the garment's washing is limited to the stained spot, he argues the vessel's scrubbing should be limited to the cooked spot. This is exactly the kind of personal reasoning the student said a משנה could overturn.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes sense

phrases.english: He said to him: It stands to reason that it is like a garment —
phrases.notes: Here רמי בר חמא is the one speaking.

phrases.english: just as a garment does not require laundering
except in the place of the blood,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כְּלִי אֵינוֹ טָעוּן מְרִיקָה וּשְׁטִיפָה
phrases.english: so too a vessel does not require scouring and rinsing
except in the place of the cooking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the objection by giving reasoning instead of a source
steps.terutzResolutionType: Admits no explicit source; justifies the ruling by comparison to a similar law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The student thought an answer without a משנה has no backing
steps.terutzMaskana: רמי claims the comparison to a blood-stained garment is enough to support the ruling

steps.title: Blood stays put, but cooking spreads
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יהודה rejects the comparison: blood does not spread through a garment, but the absorbed taste from cooking spreads through the whole vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are they really alike? Blood does not spread, but cooking does spread!
steps.whatsHappening: The student shows that רמי's comparison does not work, because the two cases are physically different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A garment is washed only where the blood is because the blood stays in that spot. Cooking is different: what the vessel absorbs spreads through all of it, so the whole vessel is affected. The comparison breaks down.

phrases.english: He said to him: Are they comparable?!
phrases.notes: Now the student, רב יצחק בר יהודה, is answering back.

phrases.english: Blood does not spread,
cooking spreads!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison offered in step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between a garment and a vessel
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Blood stays in one spot, but the absorbed taste from cooking spreads through the entire vessel

steps.title: A second refutation: a ברייתא comparing the two laws
steps.stepSummary: The student adds a second argument by quoting a ברייתא that lists ways each law, הזאה and מריקה ושטיפה, is stricter than the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, a ברייתא teaches: In some ways הזאה is stricter than מריקה ושטיפה, and in some ways מריקה ושטיפה is stricter than הזאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The student moves to a second, stronger attack: an actual written source. This line sets up the ברייתא, and its details come in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ועוד shows a second argument is coming on top of the logical one. The ברייתא's opening line already hints that the two laws do not work the same way, which undercuts רמי's comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Scouring and rinsing of a vessel that held sacrificial meat

phrases.english: And furthermore, it is taught in a baraita:
There is a stringency in sprinkling over scouring and rinsing,
phrases.notes: הזאה here means blood that splashed onto a garment, which then needs washing.

phrases.english: and a stringency in scouring and rinsing over sprinkling:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, source-based refutation after the logical one in step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רמי's ruling and his comparison to the garment
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא directly addresses the case and contradicts him (spelled out in the next steps)

steps.title: Where הזאה is stricter
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the garment law applies to both outer and inner חטאות, and even before the blood is put on the altar. מריקה ושטיפה does not apply in those cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: The stricter side of הזאה: it applies to outer חטאות and inner חטאות, and it applies before the זריקה. This is not so with מריקה ושטיפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists the first side: the cases where washing a garment applies but scrubbing a vessel does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood can splash on a garment from any חטאת, and even before the blood is thrown on the altar. A vessel only needs scrubbing after meat was cooked in it. That happens only with outer חטאות, whose meat is eaten, and only after the זריקה. This half of the ברייתא shows the two laws have different rules, setting up the decisive line.

keyTerms.meaning: Outer חטאות, whose blood is placed on the outer altar
Inner חטאות, whose blood is sprinkled inside the היכל
Throwing the blood on the altar
Which is not so (in the other case)

phrases.english: The stringency in sprinkling —
is that sprinkling applies to external sin offerings
and to internal sin offerings,
and it applies before the sprinkling on the altar;
phrases.notes: Meaning blood that splashed on a garment even before the blood was put on the altar.

phrases.english: which is not so in scouring and rinsing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first half of the ברייתא introduced in step 11
steps.raayaObject: That הזאה and מריקה ושטיפה follow different rules

steps.title: Where מריקה ושטיפה is stricter, including the whole vessel
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says מריקה ושטיפה applies to both קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים. It also says that if one cooked in only part of a vessel, the whole vessel needs it. This directly contradicts רמי בר חמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The stricter side of מריקה ושטיפה: it applies to both קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים. If one cooked in part of the vessel, the whole vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה. This is not so with הזאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other side. One of its points answers the student's original question outright: the whole vessel needs scrubbing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי ruled that only the cooked part needs מריקה ושטיפה. The ברייתא says clearly that the whole vessel does, and it even names this as a difference from the garment law. So רמי's answer from his own reasoning is overturned by a written source, just as the student warned in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the most sacred order

steps.whatToRemember: If a קרבן was cooked in even part of a vessel, the whole vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה. This differs from a garment, where only the bloodstained spot is washed. The story proves the student's point that reasoning without a משנה can be overturned.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רמי's comparison was silly. It sounded logical. It failed because cooking spreads through the vessel and because a ברייתא explicitly rules the other way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the story. It shows why רב יצחק בר יהודה preferred רב ששת, whose answers came from a משנה or ברייתא.

phrases.english: The stringency in scouring and rinsing —
is that scouring and rinsing applies

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּקׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים בֵּין בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים,
phrases.english: both to offerings of the most sacred order and to offerings of lesser sanctity,
and if one cooked in part of the vessel —
the entire vessel requires scouring and rinsing;
which is not so in sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא; its ruling on part of a vessel refutes step 7
steps.raayaObject: That the entire vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה even if cooking was in only part of it

steps.title: רמי בר חמא accepts the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Faced with a ברייתא that openly contradicts him, רמי בר חמא concedes: if a ברייתא teaches it, it is taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it is taught in a ברייתא, then it is taught, and I accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא gives up his position. He admits that the ברייתא settles the question against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His idea was only based on logic, comparing a vessel to a garment. A ברייתא is a תנאי source, so it outranks an אמורא's reasoning. Once the ברייתא says the whole vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה, his comparison falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is taught (in a ברייתא), it is taught. An אמורא's way of accepting a source he cannot argue with.

steps.whatToRemember: The final halacha is that the whole vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה, even if only part of it was used for cooking.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it is taught, it is taught.
phrases.notes: רמי בר חמא is answering רב יצחק בר יהודה. He means: a ברייתא says it, so I can't argue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concedes to the ברייתא quoted in Step 13, which contradicted רמי בר חמא's position from Step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רמי בר חמא withdraws. The whole vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה even when only part of it was used.

steps.title: What is the source for the whole-vessel rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is behind the ברייתא's rule that the entire vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the rule is accepted, the גמרא asks where it comes from. This sets up the next step, which quotes a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule but not its source. The גמרא wants to anchor the rule in the Torah's words.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the reason? A request for the source behind a rule.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why does the whole vessel need it if only part was used?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule that Step 14 just accepted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that cooking in part of a vessel requires מריקה ושטיפה for the whole vessel.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'in a copper vessel', even in part of it
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'and if it was cooked in a copper vessel' teaches that cooking even in part of a vessel makes the whole vessel need מריקה ושטיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And if it was cooked in a copper vessel.' This means even if it was cooked in only part of the vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The Torah says the meat was cooked 'in a vessel', and the whole vessel then needs מריקה ושטיפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah speaks of cooking 'in a vessel' and does not require that the whole vessel was filled. It then applies מריקה ושטיפה to the vessel. So any cooking inside it, even in one part, obligates the whole vessel.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And if it was cooked in a copper vessel"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:21

phrases.english: – and even in part of a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְאִם בִּכְלִי נְחֹשֶׁת בֻּשָּׁלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15's question with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'in a copper vessel' teach that cooking in any part of the vessel obligates the entire vessel.

steps.title: A ברייתא extends מריקה ושטיפה from חטאת to all קדשים
steps.stepSummary: Turning to the משנה's line about קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים, the גמרא quotes a ברייתא. The פסוק mentions חטאת, but 'קדש קדשים היא' extends the law to all קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Both קדשי קדשים and so on.' The רבנן taught: 'חטאת' teaches me only about a חטאת. Where do we learn it for all קדשים? The פסוק says: 'It is most holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, the rule that both levels of קדשים need מריקה ושטיפה. It brings a ברייתא that widens the law from חטאת to all קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section on מריקה ושטיפה opens by calling itself the law of the חטאת, which sounds limited to a חטאת. The ברייתא uses the words 'קדש קדשים היא' to include all other קדשים. This matches the משנה's wide rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the most holy level (like חטאת and אשם)
I only have (this case); a phrase that opens a search for a wider source
The verse teaches; introduces the proving words of a פסוק

phrases.english: Both offerings of the most sacred order, etc.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״חַטָּאת״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא חַטָּאת,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: "Sin offering" – I have only a sin offering;
phrases.notes: From ויקרא 6:18, 'this is the law of the חטאת.'

phrases.english: from where do I know all sacrificial offerings?
The verse says: "It is most holy."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:22

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה's line that the law covers both קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מריקה ושטיפה applies not just to a חטאת but to all קדשים, learned from 'קדש קדשים היא'.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: 'אותה' leaves out תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether תרומה might be included too. The word 'אותה' excludes it, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think I should include תרומה as well. The פסוק says 'it', which leaves out תרומה. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. After including all קדשים, it makes sure the law does not stretch to תרומה, and it names רבי יהודה as the author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה is also holy and eaten only by כהנים, so one might think its pots also need מריקה ושטיפה. The limiting word 'אותה' ('it') blocks that. In רבי יהודה's view the law covers all קדשים, including קדשים קלים, but not תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think; introduces a possible but wrong reading
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Might I include teruma as well?
The verse says: "It" – excluding teruma.
phrases.notes: From ויקרא 6:22, 'every male among the כהנים may eat it.'

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the wide inclusion of Step 17 so that it does not reach תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, all קדשים need מריקה ושטיפה, but vessels used for תרומה do not.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: only קדשי קדשים need it
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that only קדשי קדשים need מריקה ושטיפה, not קדשים קלים, because the פסוק says 'קדש קדשים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: קדשי קדשים need מריקה ושטיפה, and קדשים קלים do not. This is because it is written 'most holy': קדשי קדשים, yes; קדשים קלים, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second opinion. רבי שמעון reads the same words, 'קדש קדשים', as a limit instead of an inclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה read 'קדש קדשים היא' as widening the law past חטאת to all קדשים. רבי שמעון reads it as narrowing: only offerings that are truly קדשי קדשים count. So for him קדשים קלים are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Scouring and rinsing a vessel in which קדשים were cooked

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים use the same words 'קדש קדשים'. רבי יהודה uses them to include all קדשים, while רבי שמעון uses them to exclude קדשים קלים.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים טְעוּנִין מְרִיקָה וּשְׁטִיפָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Offerings of the most sacred order require scouring and rinsing;

phrases.aramaic: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים אֵינָן טְעוּנִין מְרִיקָה וּשְׁטִיפָה.
phrases.english: offerings of lesser sanctity do not require scouring and rinsing.
As it is written: "Most holy" –

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים אֵין, קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים לָא.
phrases.english: offerings of the most sacred order, yes; offerings of lesser sanctity, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing opinion to רבי יהודה's view in Steps 17-18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only קדשי קדשים need מריקה ושטיפה; קדשים קלים do not.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reasoning?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gave רבי שמעון's source. The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה knows that קדשים קלים are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה includes קדשים קלים. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's reading of 'קדש קדשים' sounds like the simple meaning. So the גמרא needs to explain how רבי יהודה can include the lesser offerings.

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי שמעון's clear source, asks for the basis of רבי יהודה's wider view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יהודה derives that קדשים קלים also need מריקה ושטיפה.

steps.title: Excluding תרומה proves קדשים קלים are included
steps.stepSummary: Since the Torah needed 'אותה' to leave out תרומה, it must be that קדשים קלים are included. Otherwise תרומה would obviously be left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since 'it' was needed to leave out תרומה, we can conclude that קדשים קלים do need מריקה ושטיפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יהודה. The Torah would not bother to exclude תרומה unless the lesser קדשים were already included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even קדשים קלים were left out, then תרומה, which is less holy, would surely be left out too, and there would be no need for 'אותה'. The fact that the Torah used a word to exclude תרומה shows that the line is drawn below קדשים קלים. So קדשים קלים are included.

phrases.english: Since "it" was needed to exclude teruma,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים טְעוּנִין מְרִיקָה וּשְׁטִיפָה.
phrases.english: by inference, offerings of lesser sanctity require scouring and rinsing.
phrases.notes: If קדשים קלים were left out, תרומה would obviously be left out too, with no word needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by reasoning from the exclusion of תרומה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The need to exclude תרומה with 'אותה' shows that קדשים קלים are included in מריקה ושטיפה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון uses 'אותה' for something else
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that 'אותה' is not about תרומה at all. It teaches a different law, the one the גמרא already learned earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון would tell you: 'it' teaches what we said earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון against רבי יהודה's proof. For רבי שמעון, the word 'אותה' is used for a different teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's proof depends on 'אותה' being needed to exclude תרומה. רבי שמעון says the word has a different job, so nothing can be inferred about קדשים קלים. His limit, only קדשי קדשים, stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you; introduces how a תנא would answer

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: all קדשים need מריקה ושטיפה, but not תרומה. רבי שמעון: only קדשי קדשים need it, and he uses 'אותה' for a different teaching.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon would say to you:
"It" is needed for what we said earlier.
phrases.notes: Earlier in this perek, 'אותה' was used to leave out a חטאת that became פסול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Neutralizes Step 21's proof by giving 'אותה' a different purpose for רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the extra word to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'אותה' excludes תרומה, קדשים קלים must be included, so רבי שמעון seems refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, 'אותה' teaches the earlier law, so no inference about קדשים קלים can be made, and his view stands.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that a תרומה pot does need cleaning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how 'אותה' could leave תרומה out of מריקה ושטיפה, since a ברייתא teaches that a pot used for תרומה gives off its taste and so must be cleaned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that תרומה does not need rinsing and scouring? But a ברייתא teaches: a pot used to cook meat may not be used to cook milk, and if someone did, it depends on whether the meat gives taste to the milk. Likewise, a pot used for תרומה may not be used to cook חולין, and if someone did, it depends on whether the תרומה gives taste to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that תרומה is left out of the cleaning rule. It quotes a ברייתא that treats a תרומה pot like a meat pot, so its absorbed taste matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says absorbed תרומה taste can pass into חולין later cooked in the pot. If the absorbed taste matters, the pot has to be cleaned before it is used for חולין. That seems to clash with the reading that 'אותה' frees תרומה from cleaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives taste. A mixture is forbidden if the absorbed food gives its taste.
Ordinary food that is not holy

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never uses the words מריקה ושטיפה. The point is that if absorbed תרומה taste matters, the pot clearly needs some cleaning.

phrases.english: And does תרומה not need rinsing and scouring?!
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
A pot in which one cooked meat
one may not cook milk in it,
and if he did cook it, it depends on whether it gives taste.
If תרומה was cooked in it, one may not cook ordinary food in it,
and if he did cook it, it depends on whether it gives taste!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְרוּמָה לָא בָּעֲיָא שְׁטִיפָה וּמְרִיקָה?! וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim from steps 18 and 21 that 'אותה' leaves תרומה out of the cleaning rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'אותה' frees תרומה from מריקה ושטיפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that absorbed תרומה taste can pass into other food. So a תרומה pot must need cleaning.

steps.title: אביי: For תרומה, only the part of the pot that was used needs cleaning
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that 'אותה' only frees תרומה from the rule that the whole vessel must be cleaned. For תרומה, only the spot where it was cooked needs cleaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The exclusion is needed only for what the Master said: if someone cooked in part of a vessel, the whole vessel needs scouring and rinsing. But for תרומה, only the place where it was cooked needs it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. תרומה does need cleaning, and the verse only leaves it out of one strict detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים, cooking in even part of a vessel makes the whole vessel need מריקה ושטיפה. אביי says 'אותה' takes תרומה out of that extra strictness, so only the cooked area needs cleaning. This fits with the ברייתא, which only shows that some cleaning is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this. The phrase narrows a teaching to one specific point.
The place of cooking, meaning the spot that actually touched the food

phrases.english: אביי said:
It is needed only for what the Master said:
phrases.notes: 'It' means the word 'אותה' that leaves תרומה out.

phrases.english: If one cooked in part of a vessel,
the whole vessel requires scouring and rinsing.
But this, תרומה,
needs only the place of cooking to be cleaned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, לָא צְרִיכָא אֶלָּא לִדְאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23 by narrowing what 'אותה' leaves out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the exclusion: תרומה is freed from one detail, not from cleaning altogether.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומה needs cleaning only where it was cooked, not the whole vessel.

steps.title: רבא: A תרומה pot may be cleaned even with wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that 'אותה' only frees תרומה from the rule that cleaning must be done with water. A תרומה pot may be cleaned even with wine or diluted wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The exclusion is needed only for what the Master said: 'in water' and not in wine, 'in water' and not in diluted wine. But this, תרומה, may be cleaned even in wine and even in diluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the same challenge. He picks a different detail that 'אותה' takes away from תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קדשים, the word 'במים' requires plain water, so wine or diluted wine is not acceptable. רבא says תרומה still needs cleaning, but any of these liquids will do. Like אביי, he keeps the ברייתא in place and only changes which detail is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: In water, a word from the פסוק about scouring and rinsing

phrases.english: רבא said:
It is needed only for what the Master said:
'In water' and not in wine,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:21

phrases.english: 'in water' and not in diluted wine.
But this one, תרומה, may be cleaned even in wine and even in diluted wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, לָא צְרִיכָא אֶלָּא לִדְאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than אביי to the same קשיא from step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the exclusion to the type of liquid used.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומה needs cleaning, but wine or diluted wine is also acceptable.

steps.title: רבה בר עולא: A תרומה pot may be cleaned even with hot water
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא says that 'אותה' only frees תרומה from the rule that scouring and rinsing must be done with cold water. A תרומה pot may be cleaned even with hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: The exclusion is needed only for what the Master said: scouring and rinsing are done with cold water. But this, תרומה, may be cleaned even with hot water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא gives a third answer to the same challenge. He picks yet another detail that 'אותה' takes away from תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קדשים, the scouring and rinsing must be done with cold water. רבה בר עולא says that for תרומה, hot water is also enough. All three אמוראים agree that a תרומה pot needs cleaning, as the ברייתא shows. They disagree only about which detail 'אותה' removes.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that a pot used for תרומה must be cleaned. The word 'אותה' only frees it from one strict detail of the קדשים cleaning rule. According to אביי the detail is the whole vessel, according to רבא it is water only, and according to רבה בר עולא it is cold water.

phrases.english: רבה בר עולא said:
It is needed only for what the Master said:
Scouring and rinsing are done with cold water.
But this one, תרומה, may be cleaned even with hot water.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא אָמַר, לָא צְרִיכָא אֶלָּא לִדְאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer, different from אביי and רבא, to the קשיא from step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the exclusion to the temperature of the water.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומה needs cleaning, but hot water is also acceptable.

steps.title: Hot water exemption does not fit the view that scouring is done with hot water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה בר עולא's answer. It works for the view that both מריקה and שטיפה are done with cold water. But for the view that מריקה is done with hot water, what does 'אותה' exempt for תרומה?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is fine for the one who says scouring and rinsing are both done with cold water. But for the one who says scouring is done with hot water and rinsing with cold water, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning רבה בר עולא's answer from Step 26. It says the answer only works for one opinion about how the cleaning is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר עולא said a תרומה pot may be cleaned with hot water alone, unlike a קדשים pot, which needs cold water. But one opinion holds that the Torah's מריקה is itself the hot-water purging. On that view, leaving תרומה out of מריקה ושטיפה would free it from the hot-water purging too. That clashes with the ברייתא in step 23, which shows a תרומה pot must be purged.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (said before raising a problem for another view)
According to the one who says

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says:
scouring and rinsing are both done with cold water;
but according to the one who says:
scouring is done with hot water and rinsing with cold water –
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְרִיקָה וּשְׁטִיפָה בְּצוֹנֵן אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה בר עולא's answer in Step 26 by showing it fits only one opinion about the water used for cleaning.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר עולא's explanation that 'אותה' lets a תרומה pot be cleaned with hot water.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the Torah's מריקה is the hot-water purging, then excluding תרומה from מריקה ושטיפה would exempt it from purging. That contradicts the ברייתא that a תרומה pot must be purged.

steps.title: For that view, תרומה is exempt from the extra rinsing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that according to the view of hot-water מריקה, 'אותה' exempts תרומה from the additional שטיפה that the Torah requires after the scouring.
steps.simpleTranslation: The extra rinsing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 27 in two words. On that view, a תרומה pot is exempt from the extra rinsing step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this view, מריקה and שטיפה are two separate steps: hot-water scouring, then a cold-water rinse. A תרומה pot still needs the scouring, which fits the ברייתא that it must be cleaned. But 'אותה' frees it from the second, extra rinse.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It': the word in the פסוק that the גמרא reads as leaving out תרומה
The portion given to a כהן; a pot used for it is the case being discussed

steps.whatToRemember: Every answer in this section (אביי, רבא, רבה בר עולא, and this last one) agrees on one thing. A תרומה pot still needs some cleaning, and 'אותה' only lightens one detail of מריקה ושטיפה.

phrases.english: The extra rinsing.
phrases.notes: The גמרא means that 'אותה' exempts a תרומה pot from this extra rinse only. It still needs the scouring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the exemption: on this view, a different detail is exempted for תרומה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: On the hot-water view, 'אותה' seemed to exempt תרומה from nothing at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: On the hot-water view, 'אותה' exempts תרומה from the second, extra cold-water rinse. The scouring is still required.

steps.title: The משנה: may one pot be used for the whole רגל?
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון says that if someone cooked in a pot at the start of the רגל, he may keep cooking in it all רגל long. חכמים say he must scour and rinse it before the time for eating the offering ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: if someone cooked in it at the start of the festival, he may cook in it the whole festival. The חכמים say: only until the time for eating ends.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי טרפון and חכמים argue about how long a pot may be used before it must be scoured and rinsed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון lets the pot be used for the whole רגל without cleaning it after every offering. חכמים do not allow this. The pot must be cleaned before the eating time of the offering cooked in it is over.

keyTerms.meaning: The time during which the offering may be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: חכמים do not mean you must stop cooking. They mean the pot must be scoured and rinsed before the eating time of that offering runs out.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Tarfon says:
if he cooked from the beginning of the festival –
phrases.notes: He cooked an offering in a copper pot, the kind of pot that needs scouring and rinsing.

phrases.english: he may cook in it the whole festival.
And the Rabbis say: until the time of eating.
phrases.notes: They mean the pot must be scoured and rinsed before the eating time for that offering ends.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר בִּישֵּׁל מִתְּחִילַּת הָרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the end of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון: a pot used at the start of the רגל may be used all רגל. חכמים: it must be scoured and rinsed before the offering's eating time ends.

steps.title: What scouring and rinsing are, and that both use cold water
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines מריקה as like scouring the inside of a cup, and שטיפה as like rinsing the outside of a cup. Both are done with cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Scouring and rinsing: scouring is like scouring a cup, and rinsing is like rinsing a cup. Scouring and rinsing are done with cold water.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how מריקה and שטיפה are done. It compares them to cleaning a cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מריקה is like cleaning the inside of a cup that wine stuck to. שטיפה is like rinsing the outside of the cup. The משנה ends by saying both are done with cold water. This matches the opinion the גמרא mentioned in Step 27.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line of the משנה is the source for the view that both מריקה and שטיפה are done with cold water. That is one side of the debate the גמרא used in Step 27.

phrases.english: Scouring and rinsing –
scouring is like the scouring of a cup,
phrases.notes: This means cleaning the inside of a cup, the way you scrub off wine that stuck to it.

phrases.english: and rinsing is like the rinsing of a cup.
phrases.notes: This means washing the outside of the cup.

phrases.english: Scouring and rinsing are with cold water.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרִיקָה כִּמְרִיקַת הַכּוֹס וּשְׁטִיפָה כִּשְׁטִיפַת הַכּוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by defining the cleaning that Step 29 required.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מריקה is like scouring the inside of a cup, and שטיפה is like rinsing its outside. Both are done with cold water.
